title: 饮中八仙歌
title_en: Song of the Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup
author: 杜甫

text_note.zh: 这里按通行本。语料有两处不同：“称避贤”作“称世贤”，“雄辩”作“雄辨”。“避贤”出自李适之自己的诗句“避贤初罢相”，通行本多作“避贤”。另外，“曲车”的“曲”是“麴”（酒曲）的简化字。
text_note.en: We follow the common editions. The corpus differs in two places: it has "praised as worthy by the world" where common editions have bì xián, "making way for the worthy", and it writes the word for debate with a look-alike character. Bì xián comes from Li Shizhi's own line about stepping down as chief minister "to make way for the worthy". Also, qū in qū chē is the simplified form of the word for the yeast used to make wine.

readings.zh: 斗：古代的酒器，也是容量单位，读 dǒu，不读 dòu。
readings.en: dǒu: a wine vessel, also a unit of measure. Read dǒu, not dòu.

readings.zh: 朝天：朝见皇帝，朝读 cháo。
readings.en: cháo tiān: to go to court and see the emperor. Read cháo.

readings.zh: 曲车：装酒曲的车，曲读 qū。
readings.en: qū chē: a cart carrying wine yeast. Read qū.
zuǒ xiàng: the Chief Minister of the Left. Read xiàng.
xìng: high spirits, the mood for something. Read xìng.

readings.zh: 乐圣：喜欢喝清酒，乐读 lè。
readings.en: lè shèng: to enjoy clear wine. Here lè means to enjoy.
shào nián: a young man. Read shào.

readings.zh: 长斋：长期吃素，长读 cháng。
readings.en: cháng zhāi: keeping a meatless diet for a long time. Read cháng.
chuán: to be passed on, to spread. Read chuán.

glosses.zh: 知章：贺知章，唐代诗人，喜欢喝酒，为人豪放。他是浙江人，那里的人习惯坐船。
glosses.en: Zhizhang: He Zhizhang, a Tang poet who loved wine and was free-spirited. He came from Zhejiang, where people were used to boats.

glosses.zh: 似乘船：喝醉了骑在马上摇摇晃晃，像坐船一样。
glosses.en: sì chéng chuán: drunk on horseback, swaying as if on a boat.

glosses.zh: 眼花：喝醉了眼睛看不清。
glosses.en: yǎn huā: blurry-eyed from drink.

glosses.zh: 水底眠：掉进井里，竟然就在井底睡着了。这是夸张的说法。
glosses.en: shuǐ dǐ mián: falling into a well and simply sleeping at the bottom. It is a playful exaggeration.

glosses.zh: 汝阳：汝阳王李琎，唐玄宗的侄子。
glosses.en: Ruyang: Li Jin, the Prince of Ruyang, a nephew of Emperor Xuanzong.

glosses.zh: 三斗：喝了三斗酒。斗，盛酒的器具。
glosses.en: sān dǒu: three measures of wine. A dǒu is a wine vessel.

glosses.zh: 朝天：去朝见皇帝。
glosses.en: cháo tiān: to go to court to see the emperor.

glosses.zh: 曲车：装着酒曲的车。酒曲是用来酿酒的东西，闻起来有酒香。
glosses.en: qū chē: a cart of wine yeast, the stuff used to make wine, which smells of wine.

glosses.zh: 流涎：流口水。
glosses.en: liú xián: to drool.

glosses.zh: 移封：把封地换到别处。古代王爷有自己的封地。
glosses.en: yí fēng: to move one's fief. Princes long ago were given land of their own to rule.

glosses.zh: 酒泉：酒泉郡，在今甘肃。传说那里城下有泉，泉水像酒一样。
glosses.en: Jiuquan: "Wine Spring", a place in today's Gansu. Legend says a spring there tasted like wine.

glosses.zh: 左相：左丞相李适之，是朝中的大官。
glosses.en: zuǒ xiàng: Li Shizhi, Chief Minister of the Left, a high official at court.

glosses.zh: 日兴：每天的酒兴。
glosses.en: rì xìng: his daily urge to drink.

glosses.zh: 长鲸：巨大的鲸鱼。
glosses.en: cháng jīng: a huge whale.

glosses.zh: 百川：许多条河流。
glosses.en: bǎi chuān: a hundred rivers.

glosses.zh: 衔杯：嘴里含着酒杯，就是喝酒。
glosses.en: xián bēi: holding a cup to the lips, drinking.

glosses.zh: 乐圣：喜欢喝清酒。古人把清酒叫“圣人”，浊酒叫“贤人”。
glosses.en: lè shèng: enjoying clear wine. People long ago jokingly called clear wine a sage and cloudy wine a worthy man.

glosses.zh: 称避贤：说自己是给贤人让位。李适之被人排挤丢了相位，写诗说“避贤初罢相，乐圣且衔杯”，这里借用他的话，也有双关：不喝浊酒（贤人）。
glosses.en: chēng bì xián: saying he stepped aside for worthier men. Li Shizhi lost his post to a rival and wrote a poem saying he had stepped down "to make way for the worthy" and would now enjoy his cup. The line borrows his words, with a pun: he "avoids" cloudy wine too.

glosses.zh: 宗之：崔宗之，当时的一位贵族青年。
glosses.en: Zongzhi: Cui Zongzhi, a young nobleman of the time.

glosses.zh: 潇洒：自然大方，不拘束。
glosses.en: xiāo sǎ: easy, natural and carefree.

glosses.zh: 觞：酒杯。
glosses.en: shāng: a wine cup.

glosses.zh: 白眼：眼睛向上翻，露出眼白，表示看不起世俗的人。
glosses.en: bái yǎn: rolling the eyes up to show the whites, a sign of looking down on ordinary worldly people.

glosses.zh: 皎：洁白明亮。
glosses.en: jiǎo: bright and pure white.

glosses.zh: 玉树临风：像玉做的树站在风里，形容人长得好看、风度好。
glosses.en: yù shù lín fēng: like a jade tree in the wind; describes a handsome, graceful young man.

glosses.zh: 苏晋：当时的一位官员，信佛。
glosses.en: Su Jin: an official of the time who followed Buddhism.

glosses.zh: 长斋：长期吃素。
glosses.en: cháng zhāi: keeping a meatless diet for a long time.

glosses.zh: 绣佛：用丝线绣成的佛像。
glosses.en: xiù fó: an embroidered image of the Buddha.

glosses.zh: 逃禅：逃离佛门的戒律。佛教不许喝酒，他喝醉了就把戒律忘了。
glosses.en: táo chán: escaping the Buddhist rules. Buddhism forbids wine, but when he got drunk he forgot the rules.

glosses.zh: 一斗诗百篇：喝一斗酒，就能写一百首诗。夸张地说李白才思敏捷。
glosses.en: yì dǒu shī bǎi piān: one measure of wine, a hundred poems. A playful way to say how fast his talent flowed.

glosses.zh: 天子呼来不上船：皇帝叫他去，他醉得上不了船。传说唐玄宗在宫中游船，召李白来写文章，李白已经醉了。
glosses.en: tiān zǐ hū lái bú shàng chuán: the emperor called him, and he was too drunk to board the boat. Legend says Emperor Xuanzong was boating in the palace and summoned Li Bai to write, but Li Bai was already drunk.

glosses.zh: 张旭：唐代书法家，最擅长草书。
glosses.en: Zhang Xu: a Tang calligrapher, best at the cursive style.

glosses.zh: 草圣：写草书的圣手。草书是一种写得很快、连笔很多的书法。
glosses.en: cǎo shèng: the sage of cursive script. Cursive is a fast, flowing style of handwriting with joined strokes.

glosses.zh: 脱帽露顶：摘下帽子，露出头顶。古人在大官面前这样做是很不礼貌的，说明他醉后不拘礼节。
glosses.en: tuō mào lù dǐng: taking off his hat and baring his head, which was very rude before great lords long ago. It shows that drunk, he cared nothing for manners.

glosses.zh: 王公：王爷和大官。
glosses.en: wáng gōng: princes and high officials.

glosses.zh: 挥毫：挥动毛笔写字。
glosses.en: huī háo: wielding the writing brush.

glosses.zh: 如云烟：笔下的字像云烟一样飞动。
glosses.en: rú yún yān: the characters flow from his brush like clouds and mist.

glosses.zh: 焦遂：一个普通百姓，没做过官，以能喝酒、会说话出名。
glosses.en: Jiao Sui: a commoner who never held office, known for drinking and for brilliant talk.

glosses.zh: 卓然：精神焕发、与众不同的样子。
glosses.en: zhuó rán: lively and standing out from everyone.

glosses.zh: 雄辩：很有力、很有说服力的辩论。
glosses.en: xióng biàn: powerful, convincing argument.

glosses.zh: 四筵：满座的客人。筵，酒席。
glosses.en: sì yán: all the guests around the feast. Yán means a feast.

translation.zh: 贺知章喝醉了骑马，摇摇晃晃像坐船一样，
translation.en: He Zhizhang, drunk on horseback, sways as if he were on a boat;

translation.zh: 醉眼昏花掉进井里，竟在井底睡着了。
translation.en: blurry-eyed, he falls into a well and sleeps at the bottom.

translation.zh: 汝阳王喝了三斗酒才去朝见皇帝，
translation.en: The Prince of Ruyang drinks three measures before going to court,

translation.zh: 路上碰到装酒曲的车，口水都流出来了，
translation.en: meets a cart of wine yeast on the road, and drools,

translation.zh: 恨不得把封地换到酒泉去。
translation.en: wishing his lands could be moved to Wine Spring.

translation.zh: 左丞相李适之每天的酒兴，要花掉上万的钱，
translation.en: Chief Minister Li spends ten thousand coins a day on his love of wine;

translation.zh: 喝起酒来像巨鲸吞吸百条河水，
translation.en: he drinks like a great whale swallowing a hundred rivers,

translation.zh: 举着酒杯爱喝清酒，说自己是给贤人让位。
translation.en: cup in hand, he loves clear wine and says he has stepped aside for the worthy.

translation.zh: 崔宗之是个潇洒的美少年，
translation.en: Cui Zongzhi is a handsome, carefree young man;

translation.zh: 举起酒杯，翻着白眼望着青天，
translation.en: raising his cup, he rolls his eyes at the blue sky,

translation.zh: 洁白明亮，像玉树站在风里。
translation.en: bright and fine as a jade tree in the wind.

translation.zh: 苏晋长年吃素，供奉着绣成的佛像，
translation.en: Su Jin keeps a long meatless fast before an embroidered Buddha,

translation.zh: 可喝醉了，常常把佛门戒律抛在脑后。
translation.en: but when drunk, he often slips free of the Buddhist rules.

translation.zh: 李白喝一斗酒，就能写诗一百篇，
translation.en: Li Bai drinks one measure and writes a hundred poems;

translation.zh: 常常醉睡在长安街上的酒馆里。
translation.en: he sleeps in the wine shops of Chang'an's market.

translation.zh: 皇帝召他，他醉得上不了船，
translation.en: When the emperor calls, he cannot get onto the boat,

translation.zh: 还自称：“我是酒中的神仙。”
translation.en: and calls himself: "Your servant is an immortal of the wine cup."

translation.zh: 张旭喝了三杯，草书圣手的名声就传开了，
translation.en: Zhang Xu drinks three cups, and his fame as the sage of cursive spreads;

translation.zh: 他在王公贵族面前摘下帽子，露出头顶，
translation.en: before princes and lords he takes off his hat and bares his head,

translation.zh: 挥笔落在纸上，字像云烟一样飞动。
translation.en: and his brush on paper flows like clouds and mist.

translation.zh: 焦遂喝了五斗酒，才精神焕发，
translation.en: Jiao Sui drinks five measures before he truly comes alive;

translation.zh: 高谈阔论，雄辩滔滔，满座的客人都惊呆了。
translation.en: his bold talk and brilliant arguments amaze the whole feast.

background.zh: 这首诗一般认为是杜甫在长安时写的，大约在唐玄宗天宝年间，一说是天宝五载（746年）前后。那时唐朝正强盛，长安城里有许多爱喝酒、性情豪放的名人。杜甫挑了八个人，给他们每人画了一幅“醉像”，合起来叫“饮中八仙”。这八个人并不都在同一时间待在长安，杜甫是把他们放在一起来写的。
background.en: This poem is usually thought to have been written while Du Fu was in Chang'an, in the Tianbao years of Emperor Xuanzong; one view dates it to around 746. The Tang was then at its height, and Chang'an was full of famous, free-spirited people who loved wine. Du Fu picked eight of them and drew a drunken portrait of each, calling them the Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup. The eight were not all in Chang'an at the same time; Du Fu put them together in one poem.

author_note.zh: 杜甫（712—770），唐代大诗人，被人称为“诗圣”。他的诗大多沉重，写战乱和百姓的苦难。可是这首诗写在他年轻、还没经历安史之乱的时候，笔调轻松幽默，很少见。诗里的李白是杜甫的好朋友，杜甫一生写过不少想念李白的诗。
author_note.en: Du Fu (712–770) was a great Tang poet, often called the Sage of Poetry. Most of his poems are heavy, about war and the suffering of ordinary people. But this poem was written when he was younger, before the An Lushan Rebellion, and its tone is light and funny, which is rare for him. Li Bai, who appears in the poem, was Du Fu's good friend, and Du Fu wrote many poems missing him.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像一组漫画，一个人一格，八个人八格。贺知章醉得骑马像坐船，掉进井里还睡得着；汝阳王看见酒曲车就流口水；左丞相喝酒像鲸鱼吸水；崔宗之翻着白眼，帅得像玉树；苏晋明明吃素念佛，一醉就忘了戒律；李白喝一斗写百篇，连皇帝叫都不理；张旭喝了三杯，当着大官的面脱帽写字；最后的焦遂是个普通人，喝足了酒，一开口全场都惊呆了。每个人的写法长短不一样，写李白用了四句，最多。全诗每一句都押韵，读起来一气呵成，又快又热闹。读的时候可以想象盛唐的长安：人们自由自在，才华横溢，连喝醉的样子都那么可爱。
appreciation.en: This poem is like a comic strip, one panel per person, eight panels in all. He Zhizhang is so drunk that riding a horse feels like a boat, and he can sleep at the bottom of a well. The Prince of Ruyang drools at the sight of a wine-yeast cart. The chief minister drinks like a whale sucking up rivers. Cui Zongzhi rolls his eyes, handsome as a jade tree. Su Jin keeps a Buddhist fast, yet forgets the rules once he is drunk. Li Bai writes a hundred poems on one measure of wine and ignores even the emperor's call. Zhang Xu, after three cups, bares his head before great lords and writes. Last is Jiao Sui, a commoner: once he has had enough wine, everyone is stunned when he speaks. Each portrait has a different length; Li Bai gets four lines, the most. Every line rhymes, so the poem rushes along fast and lively. Picture Chang'an at the height of the Tang: people free and full of talent, charming even when drunk.
